uncited: Generates a shuffled permutation table of size 512 using a seeded random shuffle, then duplicates the first 256 entries to avoid modulo operations during hash-based pseudo-random number generation.

It serves as the foundational data structure for [Hash-based Pseudo-Random Number Generator](2896-hash-based-pseudo-random-number-generator.md), ensuring deterministic yet uniformly distributed indices for noise functions.

Unlike [Deterministic Integer Hashing](4149-deterministic-integer-hashing.md) which computes hashes on the fly, this method pre-computes a lookup table, trading memory for computational speed and avoiding expensive bitwise operations or trigonometric functions during ray generation.
- `m_perm`: An integer array of size 512 containing a shuffled permutation of integers $0 \dots 255$, with the first half duplicated.
The first 256 entries are a permutation of $0 \dots 255$.
The next 256 entries are identical to the first 256.
Perform a Fisher-Yates shuffle on the first `SIZE` entries using the provided `seed` to generate pseudo-random numbers.
Generate a pseudo-random integer `j` in the range $[0, i]$ using the seeded RNG.
- **Seed Collision:** Different seeds produce different permutations, but if the seed is not properly initialized, the table may be non-deterministic across runs.
- **Modulo Avoidance:** The duplication step is critical.
When accessing the table with an index $k$, the code typically uses `perm[k & 255]` (bitwise AND) instead of `perm[k % 256]`.
This requires the table to have at least 256 valid entries starting from index 0, which the duplication ensures.
If the table were not duplicated, indices $256 \dots 511$ would be out of bounds or require modulo.
No floating-point precision issues arise during generation.
Converts the CPU-side permutation array into GPU-readable textures for 1D and 2D noise lookups.
The 1D permutation table is stored in a `Texture2D` of dimensions `(SIZE, 1)` with `Alpha8` format.
The pixel at coordinate $(x, 1)$ is set to `Color(0, 0, 0, m_perm[x] / (SIZE - 1))`.
This normalization maps the integer indices $0 \dots 255$ to the floating-point range $[0, 1]$ suitable for GPU texture sampling.
This allows the noise function to be evaluated entirely on the GPU using texture lookups, which can be faster than computing hashes in shader code on some hardware architectures.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ where $N=256$.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ integers. 512 integers = 2 KB.
Faster than computing sine/dot product hashes per sample.
Less flexible than on-the-fly hashing if the hash function needs to change dynamically.
Originated in the context of GPU-based marching cubes and noise generation, specifically in the [Scrawk/Marching-Cubes-On-The-GPU](https://github.com/Scrawk/Marching-Cubes-On-The-GPU) repository.
It is a standard technique in procedural noise generation to provide a fast, deterministic way to map integer coordinates to pseudo-random values.
